## Dependency and compatibility profiles

Each entry names a profile. Apply that profile along with the entry's notes. Related source paths are inspection pointers, not a promise that all dependencies have been resolved. Copy the listed bundle, inspect its links and invoked skills recursively, then adapt to the consuming project.

### addy-skill

Markdown-first engineering workflow. Copy the complete skill folder; inspect repo-level references and other named skills. Shared checklists sit outside individual folders, so copy needed checklists and rewrite ../../references paths. Most workflows transfer across agents; browser-testing requires Chrome DevTools MCP, and delegation or source lookup steps need available equivalents. Read examples against the project stack; do not assume TypeScript. Inspect the source LICENSE.

Inspect: [repos/addyosmani-agent-skills/references](repos/addyosmani-agent-skills/references), [repos/addyosmani-agent-skills/LICENSE](repos/addyosmani-agent-skills/LICENSE).

### matt-skill

Promoted composable workflow. Copy the whole skill folder, including adjacent Markdown, scripts, and agents/openai.yaml where present. Many invoke sibling skills through the Skill tool. Engineering flows may assume issue-tracker, triage, glossary, and ADR configuration from setup-matt-pocock-skills. Adapt these to existing project conventions. Preserve intentional user-only invocation; inspect disable-model-invocation and allow_implicit_invocation rather than enabling everything automatically.

Inspect: [repos/mattpocock-skills/LICENSE](repos/mattpocock-skills/LICENSE), [repos/mattpocock-skills/skills/engineering/setup-matt-pocock-skills](repos/mattpocock-skills/skills/engineering/setup-matt-pocock-skills), [repos/mattpocock-skills/.agents/invocation.md](repos/mattpocock-skills/.agents/invocation.md).

### pstack-skill

Canonical Cursor source. Copy the complete skill folder and recursively inspect named sibling skills, principle skills, agents, references, scripts, and playbooks. For Claude Code, inspect the generated counterpart under repos/cursor-plugins/harness/pstack/claude-code before selecting the version to copy; retain its adapter. Codex needs tool, delegation, model, path, and invocation adaptation against its actual session capabilities. This is not a drop-in cross-agent installation.

Inspect: [repos/cursor-plugins/pstack/LICENSE](repos/cursor-plugins/pstack/LICENSE), [repos/cursor-plugins/pstack/docs/harness/claude-code.md](repos/cursor-plugins/pstack/docs/harness/claude-code.md).

### cursor-workflow

Cursor-origin workflow or persona. Inspect its whole folder and manifest for invoked agents, commands, rules, hooks, scripts, and services. Translate Cursor tool names and environment assumptions to the actual consuming agent. Delegation or model choices are optional capabilities to assess, not installation prerequisites to impose on every project. Keep existing approval and Git rules.

### integration

Service integration bundle. Inspect README, manifest, mcp.json where present, rules, skills, and LICENSE. Copy only needed configuration and guidance; adapt to the consuming client schema. Requires the actual service, permissions, credentials or OAuth flow, and a supported MCP transport. Client/backend-managed auth and placeholders do not necessarily transfer to Claude Code or Codex; resolve them explicitly. Catalog inclusion does not verify live endpoints, access, or production maturity.

### source-tooling

Source-specific maintenance, validation, evaluation, or packaging material. Inspect scripts and local imports together with relevant manifests, fixtures, schemas, and source instructions. Adapt assumptions about directory layout and naming. Evaluation agents may spend tokens; installers, linkers, hooks, and generators may write files. Copying is allowed under project rules; running them requires inspection and the normal project permissions. Root agent instructions are maintenance context, not project starter templates.

### reference

Reusable checklist, persona, command, or documentation reference. Read the complete source and its links. Select the relevant portions, retain attribution, adapt paths and tooling, and reconcile its policies with the consuming project. A command or persona may invoke sibling skills and require supporting references; it is not necessarily standalone.

### project-toolkit-tool

Independently copyable tool folder. Copy its complete contents, including ORIGIN.md/ORIGIN.json, notices and sibling imports. Read the local README for command/configuration, exit/completeness and mutation contracts. Most tools use Python 3.10+ standard library; PHP, Bash/Git, SQLite FTS5 and service/client prerequisites are component-specific. No installation, credentials, network call or hook activation transfers with a copy. Tests use fixtures; live services and agent-runtime behavior are not certified.

Inspect: [repos/gglerum-project-agent-toolkit/provenance/README.md](repos/gglerum-project-agent-toolkit/provenance/README.md).

### project-toolkit-skill

Reusable workflow adapted from local project practice. Copy the complete skill folder with its origin/notices and the explicitly listed tool/reference bundles; preserve the relative skills/tools/references layout or rewrite links after relocation. Replace client-specific tools with available equivalents. Keep the consumer's authorization, testing, Git and shipping rules; source approvals/model defaults do not transfer.

Inspect: [repos/gglerum-project-agent-toolkit/provenance/README.md](repos/gglerum-project-agent-toolkit/provenance/README.md).

### project-toolkit-framework

Version-specific PHP/Laravel reference skill. Copy the whole folder, including rules/references and upstream licence/origin. Check the actual installed package/version against provenance and adapt documentation/MCP lookup to available tools or official docs. Consumer conventions and permissions govern. These are static reference adaptations; framework APIs and installed client behavior were not exercised end to end.

Inspect: [repos/gglerum-project-agent-toolkit/provenance/README.md](repos/gglerum-project-agent-toolkit/provenance/README.md).

### project-toolkit-reference

Reusable operational checklist or template derived from dated project practice. Copy the Markdown plus adjacent origin files. Keep source attribution and applicable licences, and adapt environment, workload and approval assumptions. The reference does not authorize executing source infrastructure/provisioning commands.

Inspect: [repos/gglerum-project-agent-toolkit/provenance/README.md](repos/gglerum-project-agent-toolkit/provenance/README.md).

### project-toolkit-maintenance

Collection-specific maintenance and validation. Use in an intact toolkit checkout, or copy the full listed context to adapt the checker. This is not an application starter or policy installer. Requires Python, Git, Bash and PHP for all checks; fixture tests do not require paid models, live services or database/daemon access. Preserve origin records and review changes before refreshing hashes.

Inspect: [repos/gglerum-project-agent-toolkit/provenance/README.md](repos/gglerum-project-agent-toolkit/provenance/README.md).

### cut-the-fluff

Warehouse-owned portable skill; copy the entire package with references, Python helpers, schemas, tests, provenance and notices. Python 3.11+ standard library; POSIX required only for approved mutation. WSL drvfs changes require Linux-hosted private state. Inventory loading profiles remain documentation-based with synthetic compatibility tests: newer numeric Claude versions or later Codex docs snapshots retain loading expectations at low confidence with a newer_version gap; older/unparseable versions and Codex binary versions have unknown loading. Claude transcript analysis and read-only pilots were exercised on real stores; unresolved dynamic file accesses qualify file-read coverage separately. Codex adapter: validated on 1 rollout, metadata shapes only; opaque outcomes and unattributable native file changes keep it partial. Twelve fresh restricted Claude sessions preserve fixture answers/discovery while routed-task API input increases; native startup/skill activation and general token savings remain unvalidated. Read the validation/runtime/change contracts. Explicit audit scope and exact user approval are required for real-project changes. No agent launcher, hooks, global installation, telemetry or service dependency.

### ponytail-skill

Single-file lazy-senior-developer skills (YAGNI, standard library first, one-line caveat at the end of each reply). Copy the whole skill folder; each is one SKILL.md with no scripts or sibling-skill invocations, but ponytail-help lists the other five and the /ponytail level switch (lite/full/ultra) only persists when the Claude/Codex hooks are installed, so otherwise level changes last for the session at most. ponytail-gain prints benchmark figures from the source's benchmarks/results folder; the figures are the vendor's own, not a measurement of the consuming project. The policy of minimal diffs and small asserted self-checks can conflict with a project's own testing or architecture rules: pick one coherent policy. Inspect the source LICENSE (MIT) and keep attribution.

Inspect: [repos/dietrichgebert-ponytail/LICENSE](repos/dietrichgebert-ponytail/LICENSE), [repos/dietrichgebert-ponytail/benchmarks/results](repos/dietrichgebert-ponytail/benchmarks/results).

### ponytail-host-adapter

Host-specific distribution adapters around the canonical skills. Hooks are Node.js (CommonJS, standard library only) and need CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT or an equivalent root variable, path rewrites after relocation, and explicit user approval before being enabled. The Claude/Codex hooks write a mode flag under the agent config directory and may edit statusline settings. The optional band ledger (claude-band.json, hooks/band, ponytail-band-import.js) writes a per-project CSV under ~/.config/ponytail and can post each turn's row to a user-configured webhook: leave it out unless wanted and approved. Plugin manifests and marketplace files describe upstream installation and publishing; read them as reference, do not install or publish from the warehouse.

Inspect: [repos/dietrichgebert-ponytail/LICENSE](repos/dietrichgebert-ponytail/LICENSE), [repos/dietrichgebert-ponytail/docs/agent-portability.md](repos/dietrichgebert-ponytail/docs/agent-portability.md).

## Validation

Run `python3 scripts/warehouse.py check` for source drift and structural integrity. See [README.md](README.md#maintenance) for the review process and [validation/SMOKE.md](validation/SMOKE.md) for representative discovery/copy checks. No upstream agent workflow or live integration is certified by these checks.
